title: CARTGen-IR: Synthetic Tabular Data Generation for Imbalanced Regression
summary: Adapts classification and regression trees to the imbalanced-regression setting, where the rare cases sit in a continuous target's sparse regions rather than in a minority class, generating synthetic cases weighted toward those regions and testing whether downstream regressors improve there. Three SDV synthesizers are among the compared generators run at their default settings: CTGAN, TVAE and CopulaGAN, with the paper citing the SDV paper itself for CopulaGAN.
evidence: the related-work section states that GANs and VAEs have been explored for synthetic data generation and that models like TVAE, CTGAN (both reference 29), CopulaGAN (reference 19) and TabDDPM have been widely studied for synthetic case generation but lack specific focus on imbalanced regression; the same section notes that a CART approach applied to survival analysis in oncology trials outperformed Random Forests, Bayesian Networks and CTGAN particularly in low-data settings; the experimental hyperparameter table lists TVAE, CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TabDDPM each with no tuned parameters, meaning they were run at defaults against the tuned CARTGen-IR; reference 29 is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni and reference 19 is Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni, The Synthetic Data Vault, DSAA 2016

title: Syntheval: a framework for detailed utility and privacy evaluation of tabular synthetic data
summary: Presents SynthEval, an evaluation framework for tabular synthetic data that treats utility and privacy as a panel of thirty metrics rather than a single score, handles mixed types without forcing an encoding, and lets users assemble and rank their own metric sets. SDV appears on both sides: SDMetrics is one of the four existing frameworks compared against, credited with quality and diagnostic reports but judged limited to high-level dataset similarity, and CTGAN is one of the four generators run through synthcity to produce the data the framework is demonstrated on.
evidence: the framework comparison table sets SynthEval against SynthCity, SDMetrics, TableEvaluator and DataSynthesizer on metric count, ease of use, configurability, extensibility, ranking and mixed-type strategy, giving SDMetrics 17 metrics; the accompanying text states that SDMetrics, by DataCebo, Inc. (2023), allows users to generate quality and diagnostic reports as well as column-level figures for visual comparison, and that its selection of metrics is mostly limited to high-level dataset similarity; the experimental section states that to produce synthetic data the authors use four readily available generators, two GAN models, ADS-GAN and CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019), implemented through synthcity, plus DataSynthesizer for a Bayesian network and Synthpop CART models; the results tables carry CTGAN rows on the full metric panel for both the standard and privacy-boosted model runs

title: Housing GANs: Deep Generation of Housing Market Data
summary: Applies tabular adversarial generation to US housing market records so that price and regional data can be shared without privacy concerns, sampled on demand under user-specified conditions, and used to explore hypothetical market scenarios that the observed record does not cover. The model the paper calls Housing GANs is CTGAN applied to this domain: the methodology reproduces Xu et al.'s mode-specific normalization, the cond vector definition and the log-frequency training-by-sampling scheme as the machinery it uses, with no architectural change proposed.
affiliations: University of Koblenz and Landau; Rheinland-Pfälzische Technische Universität Kaiserslautern-Landau; Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam University; Daimler (Germany)
evidence: the abstract states that by leveraging the Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) introduced by Xu et al. (2019) the study generates synthetic tabular data tailored to the housing market, called Housing GANs; the methodology states that this study utilizes a mode-specific normalization approach to handle columns with complicated distributions, as in Xu et al. (2019), processing each column independently and representing each value as a one-hot mode vector plus a scalar within the mode; the same section reproduces Xu et al.'s Definition 2 for the cond vector indicating the condition on discrete columns, and states that the condition and training data are sampled on the log frequency of each category, allowing Housing GANs to evenly cover all discrete values, gathered from Xu et al. (2019). No modification to CTGAN's architecture or losses is proposed, so the name denotes the domain application rather than a variant

title: Generative adversarial networks for network traffic feature generation
summary: Generates synthetic network traffic features to relieve the shortage of labelled traffic data for security models, reproducing both categorical and continuous features and reporting how faithfully each architecture recovers the originals. Two of SDV's synthesizers are what the paper implements: CTGAN and CopulaGAN, run with SDV's reversible data transformation hyper transformer and its Gaussian copula transformer, and the paper sets out CTGAN's conditional architecture and mode-specific normalization as the design it builds the implementation on.
evidence: the stated contributions are implementing two GAN architectures suitably modelled to incorporate the reversible data transformation hyper transformer and the Gaussian copula transformer to generate synthetic network traffic data features, and reproducing realistic categorical and continuous synthetic traffic features; section 3.2, headed Conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN), states that CTGAN is based on the conditional GAN architecture combining class-label information with the generator and discriminator input and uses the Wasserstein GAN architecture, then describes normalizing the mode sample and completing the process with a one-hot vector carrying a normalized scalar in the mode position; section 3.3, headed Copula GAN, states that the copula approach has been used by Kamthe et al. to produce a variant of the CTGAN architecture, Copula GAN, combining probability integral transforms over uniform marginals, and describes the Clayton and Gumbel copulas capturing lower and upper tail dependencies

title: Optimal adjustment sets for causal query estimation in partially observed biomolecular networks
summary: Addresses which variables to condition on when estimating a causal effect in a biomolecular network that is only partially observed, showing that using every available variable can increase bias and variance, and selecting an adjustment set by simulating future datasets and comparing candidate sets on them. A tabular GAN attributed to Xu et al. is the simulator that step rests on, trained on historical observational data to approximate the true data-generating process, but the implementation run is Ashrapov's third-party library rather than the SDV one.
evidence: the methods state that where prior experimental data exist the synthetic data is constructed based on, for example, Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019), or statistical associations such as Bayesian network forward simulation; step 1 of the procedure, simulating future datasets, states that the authors approximated the true data generating process with Tabular GAN (Xu et al. 2019), trained on historical observational experimental data, preprocessing and training with default hyperparameters as described in Ashrapov (2020), after which N new samples were drawn. The named implementation is Ashrapov's tabgan library rather than sdv-dev's CTGAN, so no SDV code runs even though the method is credited to Xu et al. and is load-bearing for the paper's simulation step
needs: Convention gap, and the second instance in this lane: a paper runs a THIRD-PARTY REIMPLEMENTATION of CTGAN (Ashrapov's tabgan) as its production generator while crediting Xu et al. for the method. paper-llm-gan-energy-load-2024 in shard 95 does the same but only describes CTGAN in background, so citation_only 2 was uncontroversial there. Here the simulator is load-bearing for the paper's central procedure, which argues for importance 3, or for a separate treatment of third-party reimplementations alongside the third-party derivative question on paper-nft-data-trading-dpctgan-2025

title: Multimodal synthesis of MRI and tabular data with diffusion in a joint latent space via cross-attention
summary: Generates brain MRI volumes and the accompanying clinical table together rather than in sequence, diffusing in a joint latent space with cross-attention so that image and tabular modalities condition each other, and reports Frechet distance and precision-recall for the imaging side alongside standard tabular fidelity metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are the established unimodal tabular baselines the tabular half is measured against, with the paper reporting that it outperforms CTGAN and reaches results comparable to TVAE.
evidence: the abstract states that in the tabular modality the model outperformed CTGAN across standard evaluation metrics and achieved results comparable to TVAE, demonstrating competitive performance relative to established unimodal baselines; the evaluation section states the authors assess their multimodal latent diffusion model against three established unimodal baselines, TabSyn as a state-of-the-art diffusion-based tabular model, and CTGAN and TVAE (both reference 32), which remain widely utilized benchmarks; the results table reports Wasserstein distance, detection, alpha-precision, beta-recall and univariate and correlation distances for TVAE and CTGAN against TabSyn and the proposed model; reference 32 is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni

title: Green finance growth prediction model based on time-series conditional generative adversarial networks
summary: Forecasts green finance growth across Europe, Asia and the rest of the world from small regional panels of at most a few hundred records, using a nonlinear autoregressive neural network for the forecast itself and reporting R-squared above 96 per cent in every region. CTGAN is the middle of the model's three phases and the reason the forecast is feasible at that sample size: preliminary experiments showed augmentation was necessary, and CTGAN supplies the augmented training data the reported accuracy rests on.
affiliations: University of Prince Edward Island; Scientific Research Group in Egypt
Tunis University; Institut Supérieur de Gestion de Tunis; Zayed University
Scientific Research Group in Egypt; Egyptian Russian University; Helwan University
Cairo University; Kuwait University; Scientific Research Group in Egypt
evidence: the abstract states that CT-GANs were employed to augment the data for improved prediction accuracy and that the autoregressive networks trained with CT-GAN augmented data achieved R-squared values of 98.8, 96.6 and 99 per cent for Europe, Asia and other countries; the stated contributions include incorporating CT-GAN to address data scarcity; the background describes CT-GAN as a synthetic tabular data generator developed to solve problems present in the classic GAN; the architecture section states the model consists of three phases, data preparation, data augmentation using CT-GAN, and prediction using the time-series NAR network, and the experimental section states that preliminary experiments indicated the need for data augmentation so the authors employed CT-GAN as the final preprocessing step on regional datasets of 249, 102 and 66 records; reference 29 is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, NeurIPS 2019. The paper writes the name as CT-GAN throughout and glosses it parenthetically as likely referring to Conditional Generative Adversarial Network, which is its own imprecision rather than a different model

title: Improving Clinical Validity in Synthetic Electronic Health Record Generation Using Best-of-N Sampling: Comparative Evaluation Study
summary: Asks when clinically impossible rows in synthetic electronic health records can be fixed after generation rather than by retraining, comparing random sampling, naive clipping, best-of-N selection and strict rejection against dataset-specific validity constraints on three public clinical tables, and reporting the privacy cost of each in distance-to-closest-record concentration. CTGAN is one of the two generator backbones the whole study is built on, and CTGAN with best-of-16 selection is the configuration the paper names as the strongest overall trade-off, reaching zero constraint violations on all three datasets.
evidence: the methods state that the authors evaluated a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty and a conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) on three public clinical tabular datasets, stroke prediction, diabetes health indicators and cardiovascular disease, comparing random sampling, naive clipping and best-of-N selection for each generator; the introduction states that modern tabular generators such as WGAN-GP and CTGAN pose the practical question of when invalid outputs can be repaired by inference-time selection; the contribution summary states the authors benchmark the same selection strategy on CTGAN and show that CTGAN with best-of-16 achieves zero per cent violations across all three datasets, the strongest overall practical trade-off in the experiments; the approach is described as three stages, constraint definition, training a tabular generator backbone (WGAN-GP or CTGAN), and inference-time post hoc sampling; the results note DCR-based proximity concentration rose markedly under CTGAN selection

title: Enhancing Crop Classification Accuracy through Synthetic SAR-Optical Data Generation Using Deep Learning
summary: Tackles crop-type classification from fused synthetic aperture radar and optical satellite features, where the minority crop classes have too few labelled field samples for a classifier to learn them, by synthesizing additional samples for those classes and measuring the gain in classification accuracy. The paper is a study of CTGAN itself in this setting: CTGAN is the generation method under investigation throughout, chosen for its handling of the non-Gaussian feature distributions that polarimetric and optical features produce.
evidence: the abstract states that the research explores the effectiveness of the conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) as a synthetic data generation method based on a deep learning network, in addressing the challenge of limited training data for minority classes in crop classification using the fusion of SAR-optical data; the introduction states that one of the most important challenges is the non-Gaussian distribution of features in tabular data and that as a solution CTGAN has been developed to generate synthetic data by considering the distribution of input features, then states the paper aims to explore the potential of the CTGAN network in addressing crop classification using unbalanced tabular samples comprising optical and SAR polarimetric features; the research-process section states the study investigates the potential of the CTGAN network in agricultural product classification using SAR and optical polarimetric features. The arXiv version of this work carries a slightly different title from the published MDPI record used here

title: Joint Relational Database Generation via Graph-Conditional Diffusion Models
summary: Generates a whole relational database jointly rather than table by table, factorizing the distribution into a graph over primary and foreign keys and a graph-conditional diffusion model over the attributes, so that multi-hop inter-table dependencies survive instead of being cut by the conditional-independence assumptions earlier methods rely on. SDV sits on both sides of the evaluation: it is the statistical relational baseline, described as Gaussian-copula-based RDB synthesis, and the fidelity metrics including cardinality are computed with the SDMetrics package.
evidence: the baselines paragraph states the authors compare their model to four relational database generation methods from the literature and that SDV, reference 13, is a statistical method tailored for RDB synthesis based on Gaussian Copulas, set alongside ClavaDDPM and others; the evaluation-metrics paragraph states that to evaluate synthetic data fidelity the authors follow prior work and report metrics implemented in the SDMetrics package, reference 42, beginning with Cardinality, which compares the distribution of the number of child rows per parent row between real and synthetic data, computed for each parent-child pair and averaged; the related-work discussion notes that prior methods resorted to Markov-like conditional independence assumptions of tables or rows given their parents, which is the position SDV's relational approach occupies. Running SDMetrics as the evaluation harness outranks the comparison role, on the DP-CGANS and SDGym precedent

title: Improving the Generation and Evaluation of Synthetic Data for Downstream Medical Causal Inference
summary: Argues that synthetic medical data judged only on marginal fidelity can still mislead a downstream causal analysis, and proposes STEAM, which structures generation around a causal graph so that each variable is generated conditional on its parents, together with evaluation targets aimed at causal rather than distributional faithfulness. CTGAN is both a compared generic generator and a substrate STEAM is applied to: the results tables carry a CTGAN row and a STEAM CTGAN row side by side across the datasets, with the STEAM version reported as improving precision and treatment-effect error.
evidence: the taxonomy table places CTGAN and TVAE (both reference 97) among the generic generative models whose distributional target is the joint marginal, against the causal generative models and the paper's own STEAM; the experiments state the authors compare generic tabular data generators with their STEAM counterparts across all three datasets, choosing baselines across the major families, CTGAN, TVAE, ARF, NFlow and TabDDPM; the results tables report CTGAN at 0.889 precision and 0.586 PEHE error on ACTG against STEAM CTGAN at 0.892 and 0.436, with the takeaway that in the vast majority of cases generation via STEAM leads to better performance; reference 97 is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni
needs: STEAM is a model-agnostic wrapper applied over five interchangeable generators, yielding STEAM CTGAN among STEAM TVAE, STEAM ARF and the rest — the same shape as paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024 (shard 60), which was recorded derivative_work 4. Recorded api_user 4 here instead, on the reading that STEAM structures generation AROUND a frozen CTGAN rather than entering its losses, which is the GAN_BERT composition test. The two entries should be ruled together, and this is the third model-agnostic-wrapper case after shard 60 and paper-rule-guided-tabular-low-data-2025 in shard 71
